symptom: modelsdk/mpr/security_patch.go (PatchReconcileMemberAccesses) matched NoGeneralization keys "HasOwner"/"HasChangedBy"; the stored keys are "HasOwnerAttr"/"HasChangedByAttr", so its System.owner / System.changedBy branch never fired
cause: Not a live bug: the file had no production callers (UPDATE SECURITY and the marketplace step use the backend's ReconcileMemberAccesses in mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_security_write.go). And the dead branch encoded the OPPOSITE of the measured rule — it would preserve and add a MemberAccess for the audit associations, which mxbuild rejects
insight: Do NOT 'fix' a wrong BSON key without checking what the branch it unlocks does: here the typo was the only thing keeping dead code from writing CE0066. Re-measured on mxbuild 11.14.0, one entity with AutoOwner + AutoChangedBy, one rule: no audit MemberAccess -> 0 errors; + MemberAccess System.owner and System.changedBy -> CE0066 'Entity access is out of date' (matches ako/mxcli#554). Before fixing any function, grep for callers of every exported symbol in the file — a zero-caller file is a deletion, not a fix. Harness note for hand-injecting BSON with pymongo: element $ID must be Binary subtype 0; subtype 3 makes mx fail with the baffling "Expected '$ID' as the first property of a storage object, but got '$ID'"
